subject: cat-act-2011
citation: Cat Act 2011 (WA), Act No. 055 of 2011 — consolidated version 00-l0-01, currency start 25 September 2025, shown as Current on the register
note: Retrieved from the official register, legislation.wa.gov.au, not from a secondary site. The landing page for law_id 146861 offers one consolidated version: suffix 00-l0-01, currency start 25 Sep 2025, currency end 'Current'. The Word original is deposited beside the extract so both digests can be checked by hand. This subject already held an earlier extract of the same Act at registers/source-bundle/act-2011-55.txt, retrieved 2026-09-07 through Legal Data Hunter with no version or currency recorded; on a whitespace-normalised comparison the two agree to 0.9683 and the only blocks that differ are the endnote tables and the copyright notice, which this extract carries and that one dropped. The earlier file is left in place rather than deleted, and nothing encodes from it. Note that local_path below is relative to THIS repository (legalese/canon) while the pipeline's validator resolves local_path against the l4-ide repository root, so the digest rules will report `skip` — incident H-07 of the retail-barring-orders-bill-2025 register. UPDATED 2026-09-30: both sets of regulations made under the Act, and the Assembly Explanatory Memorandum, have been added as documents; the second reading speeches are cited but could not be retrieved. UPDATED 2026-10-01: the Cat Amendment (Local Laws) Bill 2026 (Bill 53) and its Legislative Council Explanatory Memorandum have been retrieved in full and deposited as text; the Assembly Explanatory Memorandum and Legislative Assembly Message No. 78 are held as digests only; the Bill's second reading speeches are cited and refused. The Bill's two offered prints are byte-identical.
in_force: In force. The Act was assented to on 9 November 2011 and commenced in three tranches (s. 1 and 2 on 9 Nov 2011; most of the Act on 1 Nov 2012; ss. 5, 6, 14(1), 18(1), 22-24, 26-35, 41, 49, 55-60 and 86 on 1 Nov 2013). The text deposited is the compilation in force from 25 September 2025, which the register still shows as current as at the retrieval date.

assembled.note: The artifact the encoding reads. Converted from the deposited .docx by tools/fetch/fetch-source.py's docx_text: one paragraph per line, Word's table-of-contents paragraphs dropped, headings rendered as '\tPart 2 — Registration, identification and sterilisation of cats'. Every quoted string in the L4 modules is to be taken from this file mechanically rather than retyped.

documents.title: Cat Regulations 2012
documents.made_under: Cat Act 2011 s 76 (general regulations) and the specific heads cited in each regulation
documents.why_it_matters: It is what makes the Act's delegated exemptions true. reg 9 prescribes the classes exempt from registration for ss 5(2)(c) and 9(2)(b); reg 10 the exemption from wearing a tag for s 6(2); reg 12 the registration periods for s 9(7); reg 17 the information a microchip implanter must give under s 15, including sterilisation status; reg 18 how a cat is identified as sterilised for s 19. Encoded in cat-regulations-2012.l4. Reading it retracted incident A-03.

documents.title: Cat (Uniform Local Provisions) Regulations 2013
documents.citation: Cat (Uniform Local Provisions) Regulations 2013 (WA), gazetted 31 October 2013 p. 4879-88
documents.made_under: Cat Act 2011 s 77 (regulations that operate as local laws)
documents.why_it_matters: Operates as a local law in every district: limits on the number of cats kept at premises, approval to keep more, SAT review, infringement notices. NOT ENCODED. It is a separate scheme from the Part 2 duties this subject encodes, and encoding it would need the local-government provisions in Parts 4 and 6 as well.

documents.status_in_law: A Bill before the Parliament of Western Australia. NOT LAW. Both were fetched on 2026-10-01 and are BYTE-IDENTICAL, sha256 032892c4c90977943f29668f4a8b218b4e1c1036768acece0d31feb7bae8d224. So either the Bill passed the Assembly unamended despite Consideration in Detail on 15 Sep 2026, or the second link is mislabelled. Recorded rather than resolved; see INCIDENTS.md B-01.

extract.scope: THE WHOLE DOCUMENT, not an extract: overview, clause notes for all four clauses, and the quotation of Interpretation Act 1984 s 43(7).

documents.status_in_law: Extrinsic material. Interpretation Act 1984 (WA) s 19 permits its consideration; it is not the law, and where it and the enacted words differ the words prevail.
documents.why_it_matters: It carries three things nothing else in the bundle does. (1) The Joint Standing Committee on Delegated Legislation's view that the Act's existing powers did not permit cat containment local laws, which is the WA delegated-legislation practice incident A-05 said it needed. (2) The Bill described both as providing a head of power and as clarifying existing legislation, which is incident B-01 and FORK-3. (3) The statement that several local governments had already attempted such local laws, which is what makes B-01 consequential rather than theoretical.

documents.title: Second reading speeches, Cat Amendment (Local Laws) Bill 2026
documents.citation: WA Hansard, Legislative Assembly 25 February 2026; Legislative Council 16 September 2026
documents.access_note: Refused on 2026-10-01 by three routes: scripted client (HTTP 403), same-origin fetch from inside the browser (HTTP 403, Azure WAF JS challenge page), and plain browser navigation to the page, which did not resolve past the challenge. Nothing was circumvented. These are the NEW-style Hansard URLs (/hansard/daily/<house>/<date>/<item>), distinct from the /Hansard/hansard.nsf/ PDF paths recorded against the Cat Act's own speeches; both are refused. See incident C-01.
documents.why_it_matters: The Minister's second reading speech would be the clearest available statement of whether the Bill is intended to confer a power or to declare an existing one — the question in B-01 and FORK-3. It is not held, so B-01 rests on the Explanatory Memorandum alone.

related_instruments.relevance: Supplies the time ss 5(1), 14(1) and 18(1) leave open: 'Where no time is fixed or allowed within which an act or thing shall be done, such act or thing shall be done with all convenient speed and as often as occasion arises.' The encoding depends on it — see FORK-2 and the third conjunct of each contravention rule.
Permits consideration of extrinsic material, which is the basis on which the Explanatory Memorandum is used at all.
Defines `veterinarian` and `veterinary premises` for s 3(1) of the Act and reg 9(2)(e). Not retrieved: whether a given person is a veterinarian is a fact supplied.

'Subsidiary legislation shall not be inconsistent with the provisions of the written law under which it is made, or of any Act, and subsidiary legislation shall be void to the extent of any such inconsistency.' The only provision that joins the Part 6 local-law power to the Part 2 duties this subject encodes. It is what answers incident B-03 and what makes B-01 consequential.

Expressly invoked by the Bill's new s 79(4) ('Without limiting subsection (3)(f) or the Interpretation Act 1984 section 43(7) or (8)'), and s 43(7) is quoted in full in the Bill's Explanatory Memorandum. They govern how a power to make subsidiary legislation may be exercised — in relation to a class of case, conditionally, at a specified time, in part of the State. That they were not treated as sufficient is the argument recorded in the revision to incident A-05.

s 79(2) makes a local law inapplicable outside the district unless made to apply there under s 80. s 80 is not encoded; `purports to apply outside the district` and `made to apply outside the district under section 80` are facts supplied in cat-part6-local-laws.l4.
